text: How long should I boil water to make it safe?
Bring it to a rolling boil and keep it there for 1 minute [1]. At altitudes above 2000 metres, boil for 3 minutes [1].

context.question: How long should I boil water to make it safe?

excerpts.title: Water purification
excerpts.text: Bringing water to a rolling boil for 1 minute kills pathogens. Above 2000 metres boil for 3 minutes.

excerpts.title: Solar water disinfection
excerpts.text: Clear PET bottles exposed to full sun for 6 hours.

text: How much bleach do I add to a litre of water?
Add 8 drops of household bleach per litre and wait 30 minutes before drinking [1]. Double the dose to 16 drops if the water is cloudy [1].

context.question: How much bleach do I add to a litre of water?

excerpts.title: Water chlorination
excerpts.text: Add 2 drops of unscented 5% household bleach per litre of clear water, stir, and let stand 30 minutes. Double the dose for cloudy water.

text: What is the dose of iodine tablets for water?
The library does not give a tablet dose. Follow the instructions on the packet; most brands specify a number of tablets per litre and a waiting time of about 30 minutes [1].

context.question: What is the dose of iodine tablets for water?

excerpts.title: Iodine
excerpts.text: Iodine tablets are sold with manufacturer instructions; a typical wait is 30 minutes before drinking.
